sections.title: Fill in the blanks and write the correct answers.

questions.q: Cakes without icing contain a high percentage of ________.
The base for decorated cakes is a fatless ________ or genoese.
In the rubbing-in method the ________ is rubbed into flour until the mixture looks like bread crumbs.
In the creaming method the fat should be soft but not ________.
Victoria cake is made by the ________ method.
Madeira cake has the sharp flavour of ________ and a light taste of lemon.
Swiss roll is a ________ up cake.
In Victoria cake, flour, butter and ________ are used in equal proportion.
The base of a Swiss roll is a ________ sponge.
White spots on the surface of a cake are due to too much ________.

sections.title: State whether the following statements are True or False.

questions.q: Cakes made using the creaming method have no fat.
questions.answer: False. Fat is creamed with sugar.

questions.q: In the creaming method, fat should be chilled.
questions.answer: False. The fat should be soft, not chilled.

questions.q: Victoria is a type of bread.
Preheating of ovens is not necessary.
questions.answer: False. Cakes are baked in a preheated oven.

questions.q: The base of a Swiss roll is a fatless sponge.
Flour, butter and sugar are used in equal proportion in Victoria cake.
There are no remedies to the faults in cake baking.
questions.answer: False. Each fault has a cause and a remedy.

questions.q: Cake faults are divided into two parts.
questions.answer: False. They are divided into six groups.

questions.q: Christmas cakes have lots of dry fruits.
Madeira cakes are cakes with icing.
questions.answer: False. They are cakes without icing.

questions.q: The whisking method batter should be baked immediately or it will sink.

sections.title: Answer the following questions (five points each).

questions.q: Mention one reason each for the following faults in cake: (i) white spots on cake surface (ii) cake baked with peeled top (iii) cake with flat top (iv) cracks on surface of cake (v) discoloured crumb.
questions.answer: (i) White spots: too much sugar, batter standing too long or very large sugar grains. (ii) Peeled top: insufficient mixing or too much heat from the top. (iii) Flat top: oven too cool or incorrect balance between fat and egg. (iv) Cracks on the surface: too hot an oven. (v) Discoloured crumb: too much bottom heat or too much baking powder.

questions.q: Name the four methods of making a cake and explain any two.
questions.answer: The four methods are rubbing-in, creaming, whisking and all-in-one. (i) Rubbing-in: chilled fat is cut small and rubbed into sieved flour until it looks like bread crumbs; used when the weight of fat is not more than half that of flour. (ii) All-in-one: all the ingredients are placed together in a bowl and beaten until smooth and creamy; used when quick preparation is wanted.

questions.q: Write five tips for making a good cake.
questions.answer: (i) Keep the ingredients and equipment ready and weigh them carefully. (ii) Follow the recipe exactly. (iii) Use egg and fat at room temperature. (iv) Do not open the oven door unnecessarily as the oven temperature falls. (v) Test the cake for readiness: it should be evenly browned, come away from the sides of the tin and spring back when pressed.

questions.q: Describe the steps of preparing a butter sponge.
questions.answer: (i) Sieve flour with baking powder. (ii) Cream fat and castor sugar until light, fluffy and white. (iii) Add the beaten eggs and vanilla a little at a time. (iv) Fold in the flour with a palette knife and add milk to get a dropping consistency. (v) Pour into a prepared tin, bake at 170 C for about 20 minutes and cool on a rack.
